title: 4.15 Are there any keys on the floor?
unit_title: Life at home, every day and yesterday
unit_outcome: Say where people and things are at home, talk about the lights and machines, ask what there is, describe someone's morning in order, say what you did yesterday and on which day, ask and tell the time, say how often you do things and give dates.
lesson_title: Are there any keys on the floor?
sub_lesson_title: Are there any keys on the floor?
goal: Say there are some things somewhere at home, ask Are there any…? and say there aren't any (Are there any keys on the floor? No, there aren't any.).
grammar_function: A follow-up of A1 4.15 More at Home: A1 names the floor, the stairs, the garden and a key; A1+ 4.15 says what there is in those places, adding some and any to 4.4's there is, there are and Are there…?: some in a positive sentence (There are some shoes on the stairs.), any in a question and after aren't (Are there any keys on the floor? No, there aren't any.), with How many … are there? A1 4.15's own photos of an empty floor, empty stairs and the garden are the places without the things; three new Flash photos add keys, shoes and chairs to them, and apples on a table and books on a sofa have an edit of the same place without them. An any sentence is never set against a photo of another place, where it would also be true.
prerequisite: A1 4.4 and 4.15 there is, there are, floor, stairs, garden, key; A1 5.4 some; A1+ 4.4 Is there…? / Are there…? and How many.
speaking_outcome: Link there are (THEH-rar) and say some and any unstressed before the noun (sum SHOES, enee KEYS). Do not require native-like speed.
